title: Atomic ingest ack protocol and sample-aware KV caching for structured logs
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: high-volume structured log traffic from tenant fleets is exposing two recurring operational problems: (1) duplicated or out-of-order deliveries to downstream stores (Loki/ELK) during network blips or restart windows; (2) unbounded KV cache growth when we try to keep per-request prefix state for correlation joins and prefix caching. Goal: implement an ingress-side atomic acknowledgement protocol to provide deterministic commit semantics to downstream sinks (idempotent/once semantics without heavy global coordination), and introduce a sample-aware KV caching layer that reduces memory while preserving trace/trace-span correlation for observability pipelines. The design must integrate with tracing hooks, honor per-tenant sampling policies, and be rollout-safe behind feature flags.
design_notes: High level: Each ingest gateway instance will maintain a per-tenant delivery queue and a local persistent checkpoint (RocksDB) that stores the highest contiguous offset acknowledged downstream along with a deduplication window keyed by (tenant, stream, event_id). Downstream sinks will be asked to produce an explicit ACK token (HTTP 200 + ack-id) on successful commit. Gateway will garbage-collect dedup entries only after the checkpoint advances.

Choice rationale: Exactly-once across distributed sinks is expensive (transaction coordinators or global leases). We opted for idempotent delivery + atomic ack tokens which gives practically once semantics for production sinks with much lower coordination cost. Trade-off: slightly higher local state and write amplification on the gateway; benefit: far fewer duplicated events and simpler rollback semantics.

KV cache: Instead of caching every prefix KV for every request, introduce sampling-aware retention. For high-cardinality tenants we will sample traces (configurable percent) at the time of initial ingest and mark sampled traces with a provenance flag. Sampled traces get sticky KV cache entries with a longer TTL; unsampled traces get ephemeral cache hints to enable correlation without persistent state. The sampling policy will be tenant-configurable and link to the console (Optimize recommendations).

Trace propagation: Ingest will verify and normalize incoming correlation IDs (X-Redwood-Corr, traceparent). If missing but a session footprint is present we will generate deterministic stable IDs (sha256(session_id + ingress-shard)) and mark for downstream visibility. We will not backfill synthetic IDs into historical logs.

Compatibility: Downstream Loki/ELK adapters will accept ack tokens but fall back to at-least-once when ack not supported. Feature flag toggles both the ack protocol and the sample-aware cache independently to allow staged experiments.

Observability: New metrics: ack_latency_ms (p50/p95), dedup_rate, checkpoint_lag_seconds, kv_cache_hit_ratio_by_tenant, sampled_trace_ratio. Dashboards and SLOs will be defined prior to canary rollout.

Data handling: PII redaction remains upstream to the parser; ack protocol will never expose raw payloads, only opaque ack IDs. Checkpoint entries are encrypted-at-rest using KMS-managed keys. Security review required for persistent checkpoints and dedup keys.
Open question: whether to run the RocksDB checkpoint per-tenant shard or coalesce many small tenants onto a shared shard to reduce file descriptor pressure. Prototype both and measure (see tasks).
tasks: Prototype checkpointing layer with RocksDB and idempotent dedup keys (spike) - Maya
Implement ack token flow in gateway->loki adapter with validation and retries - Liam
Add per-tenant sampling config and sample-aware KV cache TTL gating - Backend Team
Integrate tracing hook normalization and deterministic synthetic-corr generation - Tracing Team
Add metrics and Grafana dashboards for ack_latency, dedup_rate, checkpoint_lag - Observability
Load test with replay harness and failure injection (net partitions, process restarts) - SRE
Security review and KMS integration for checkpoint storage - Security
Create rollout feature flags and canary plan - Product/Platform
acceptance_criteria: Under a 5% packet-loss network simulation, duplicate deliveries to Loki must be reduced by >= 90% compared to baseline (measured per-minute duplicates)
KV cache memory per-ingest-instance must be reduced by >= 40% for large tenants with sampling=10% compared to full retention baseline
ACK latency p95 < 200ms on the canary cluster under expected load profile
No customer-facing errors introduced: 0 new 5xx errors for canary tenants during 72-hour canary run
Security sign-off from InfoSec on checkpoint encryption and retention policy
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal canary behind feature flag (only internal tenants) - 1 week
Phase 1: 5 pilot customers with low-volume write pattern - 2 weeks
Phase 2: ramp to 25% of tenant traffic with sampling defaults applied - 2 weeks
Phase 3: full production enablement and monitor 30-day regression metrics - rollout monitor and rollback playbook prepared
test_plan: Unit tests: dedup key generation, checkpoint commit/rollback, ack-id validation
Integration tests: gateway <-> loki adapter ack handshake with simulated disk and network failures
Load test: replay 20k reqs/s per gateway with mixed sizes and verify dedup reduction and checkpoint stability
Chaos: kill gateway process, restart, ensure checkpoint resumes and duplicates remain bounded
E2E: end-to-end tracing correlation preserved for sampled traces (validate in trace UI)

notes: Downstream adapters: create adapters for Loki, ElasticSearch, and S3 archival. S3 will only need eventual ack semantics (store-only).
Metric ownership: Observability team to own new metrics; link dashboards to incident playbooks for checkpoint_lag alerts.
Follow-ups: investigate a hybrid checkpoint tiering using a small in-memory LRU plus cold RocksDB tier for very low-throughput tenants to reduce disk churn.
Estimated infra cost impact: +3-6% CPU and +10-20% ephemeral NVMe usage per gateway during compaction windows; include in capacity planning for Dedicated customers.
